what: THE SAME ADDRESS, FOUR MONTHS LATER — Martha Maud and the four youngest
image: TNA/BT27/1542/00/0024 page 7, Dunvegan Castle, London 10 August 1939
note: One brace spanning all five: Wear Mrs M (44), Miss K (18), Miss C (8), Miss L (6), Mast B (2). TWO INDEPENDENT VOYAGES, FOUR MONTHS APART, GIVE THE SAME HOUSE.

This archive published that Janette "was a cinema cashier IN LODGINGS on Ridge Avenue, half a mile away". 18 RIDGE AVENUE WAS THE FAMILY'S OWN HOUSE. She was not in lodgings and she had not moved out; she was in the house her parents had just sailed from, alone, on 29 September 1939.
Country of Intended Future Permanent Residence for Martha and all four children. Not visitors, not a passage out and back. Column (8), country of last permanent residence, is ditto-marked to England.

what: *** WHY THE VOYAGES WERE NOT SWEPT END TO END ***
reading: Durban Castle 11 pages, Dunvegan Castle 15 pages
note: THE ROW HOPED A CO-PASSENGER FROM LETCHWORTH WOULD ANSWER "WHY SOUTH AFRICA". IT CANNOT. BT 27 in 1939 has NO DESTINATION-ADDRESS COLUMN — the furthest it goes is "country of intended future permanent residence", a country and nothing finer. So the set cannot say where in South Africa anybody was going, and a shared home town on a passenger list would be suggestive at best. Two pages were read in full; twenty-four were not, and this row says so rather than implying a voyage-wide negative.

what: HOW THE IMAGES WERE READ, for whoever comes next
note: The viewer's own image endpoint takes IIIF region and size parameters, so a column can be cropped and read at native resolution instead of squinting at a whole page. THE ID IS RECONSTRUCTABLE: a transcript is /transcript?id=TNA/BT27/<piece><00><sub>/<entry>, and opening it in the viewer issues an info.json naming the page id. REGION CROPS ARE REFUSED ("Access forbidden") ON A PAGE THE VIEWER HAS NOT OPENED — whole-page fetches work on any page, region crops only after the viewer has opened that page. That is an access control and it was not worked around; it is why pages were opened one at a time.

what: *** THE ADDRESS COLUMN IS A FORM REVISION, NOT A PROPERTY OF BT 27 *** — checked across three eras
note: THE PRE-WAR FORM HAS NO "LAST ADDRESS IN THE UNITED KINGDOM" AT ALL. Its columns are: Port of Embarkation · No. of Contract Ticket · Names of Passengers · Profession, Occupation or Calling · AGES BUCKETED BY NATIONALITY (English / Scotch / Irish / Foreigners, each Married, Single, Children 1-12, Infants) · Ports at which Passengers have contracted to Land. No address, no residence, no intention. A row planning to get a UK address out of BT 27 must check the era first.

what: THE SAME FORM IN 1937 AS IN 1939
image: TNA/BT27/1490/00/0047 p6, Windsor Castle, Southampton 12 March 1937
note: IDENTICAL REVISION TO THE 1939 SHEETS. (6) Last Address in the United Kingdom · (7) Profession, Occupation or Calling · (8) Country of Last Permanent Residence · (9) Country of Intended Future Permanent Residence. So Leonard's 1937 crossing sits on the same form as his parents' 1939 ones and its column (6) is readable too — NOT YET READ, and recorded here as available rather than done.

what: AND THE POSTWAR LISTS ARE NOT ONE FORM AT ALL
image: TNA/BT27/1689/00/0057 p32, USNS Gen. A. M. Patch, Southampton to New York, 6 November 1951
reading: ITEM · NAME · RANK · SER.NO. · STATUS · DESTINATION
note: A TYPED US MILITARY TRANSPORT MANIFEST filed inside BT 27. Nothing of the Board of Trade form survives on it. It carries a DESTINATION column, which the 1939 form does not — but it is a city, on a list that is not the standard form, for passengers who are not emigrants. NOT OUR FAMILY: the name on it is Carl L. Wear Jr., a USAF sergeant. Recorded because it shows the series is not homogeneous and a column present in one piece proves nothing about another.

what: *** AND THE 1937 CROSSING GIVES THE SAME HOUSE, TWO YEARS EARLIER ***
image: TNA/BT27/1490/00/0047 page 6, Windsor Castle, Southampton 12 March 1937, entry 00171
reading: Wear, Mr L A R · 20 · 18, Ridge Avenue, Letchworth, Herts. · Engineer
note: READ THE SAME DAY THE FORM SURVEY FOUND THE 1937 SHEET IS THE SAME P.M. 21 REVISION, which is the only reason it was worth opening. THREE DEPARTURES ACROSS TWENTY-NINE MONTHS — Leonard in March 1937, his father in April 1939, his mother and the four youngest in August 1939 — AND ALL THREE GIVE 18 RIDGE AVENUE. It is not an address the family happened to be at when they left. It is where they lived.

reading: Ridge Avenue written out in full
note: Both 1939 entries abbreviate to "18 Ridge Ave" with a flourish, and this archive read the word with a query against it. LEONARD'S CLERK WROTE IT OUT: "18, Ridge Avenue, Letchworth, Herts." No query remains, and the county is on the page too.

IT DOES NOT NARROW THE MOVE OUT OF 72 PIX ROAD. That bracket is still 1921 (census, Wears there) to October 1935 (a wedding report giving the house to Mr and Mrs E. S. Chapman), and it is bounded from the Pix Road side. What changes is the other end: the family was ESTABLISHED at Ridge Avenue by 12 March 1937, so the gap between leaving one house and being settled in the other is at most seventeen months. THE ELECTORAL REGISTERS FOR 1936 AND 1937 WOULD CLOSE IT, and row 136 already knows where they are.
